newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks expected to focus on politics next week.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks expected to focus on politics next week.

text.p: A dearth of economic data and corporate results next week is likely to turn the attention of the UK equity markets to domestic politics, with both major parties set to publish their election manifestos.

Even the closely watched U.S. employment data, due on April 4, is likely to have only a limited impact on UK equities since the Federal Reserve already moved to tighten credit this week with what it characterised as a pre-emptive strike.

"The immediate focus on U.S. data has dimmed a bit now that the Fed has taken action on interest rates," said NatWest Markets equity strategist David McBain. "Markets will continue to monitor U.S. economic figures, but I think we'll see domestic politics move more to the forefront."

The ruling Conservative party, lagging the Labour party by 21 percentage points in the polls, is set to release its manifesto on April 2. The Labour party will publish its policy objectives the following day.
With much already in the public domain, there is little likelihood of the documents containing enough new information to produce big market swings, dealers said.
"People will be searching for detail. In the absence of a surprise, we may just drift and consolidate around these levels," said McBain.
Andy Hartwill, stock strategist with SocGen, said he did not see much potential for upside surprises and was looking for a flat to lower market next week.
"Monetary and fiscal tightening is a given," said Hartwill.

Any indication that the ruling Conservatives are gaining ground might cause some anxiety in the market. "A hung Parliament would be the worst case," said Hartwill. "A 51-seat (Labour) majority is in the market."
The UK's FTSE 100 share index reclaimed the 4,300 level in the past week in the wake of the U.S. interest rate hike. Investors, relieved the Fed was not more aggressive, bid UK shares higher.
The market got a further boost as institutional fund managers scooped up shares, preparing for the end of the quarter, strategists and dealers said.
UK data due next week include the purchasing managers' index, consumer credit and money supply.
No major UK companies are scheduled to release results.
In the U.S., data on personal income and spending, the purchasing managers index, leading economic indicators, construction spending, factor orders and U.S. employment are due for release next week.
